# Cache-derived dynamic bucket size limit
Source: https://llms-explorer.com/tree/cache-derived-dynamic-bucket-size-limit/

# Cache-derived dynamic bucket size limit — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Cache-derived dynamic bucket size limit. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How it works

- [statement] SERVER-89233 lists 7.0.4 and 7.0.5 as affected and 8.0.5 and 8.1.0-rc0 as fix versions for pathological one-document buckets with cache-pressure closures. A prior minimum-size fix does not establish that all causes of this symptom were resolved. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-04-25) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-89233 · keywords: Cache-derived dynamic bucket size limit · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-82798
- [statement] High metadata cardinality can increase the bucket working set and cause MongoDB to enforce a smaller maximum bucket size. Increasing a bucket time span therefore does not guarantee larger buckets when the cache-derived cap is binding. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations.md · keywords: Cache-derived dynamic bucket size limit · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-69899, https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/v8.0/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] MongoDB v8.0 documents numBucketsClosedDueToCachePressure as closures caused by exceeding a dynamic bucket-size limit derived from storage-engine cache size and bucket count. It documents numBucketsClosedDueToMemoryThreshold separately for the active set exceeding the bucket catalog allocation. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/reference/command/serverstatus/ · keywords: Cache-derived dynamic bucket size limit · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/v8.0/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp, https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-69899
- [statement] SERVER-105187 says the calculation combines bucket cardinality across collections. Thus activity in other time-series collections can influence this limit; it is not solely a function of one collection's ingest rate. The reported 2023 workload also observed smaller buckets after interleaved loading across collections. (medium confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-105187 · keywords: Cache-derived dynamic bucket size limit · also: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/suboptimal-bucket-creation-in-timeseries-collection-due-to-cache-pressure/249863
- [statement] The 2023 forum report described near-singleton buckets, many cache-pressure closures, and increased storage after sustained loading. This is a workload report, not proof that every dynamic-limit closure produces a singleton bucket or that a particular tuning change will fix all deployments. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/suboptimal-bucket-creation-in-timeseries-collection-due-to-cache-pressure/249863

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] SERVER-69899 describes dynamic sizing as a response to many active buckets exceeding WiredTiger cache capacity and making each document write trigger disk I/O. The half-cache target is a working-set sizing policy with disk-usage and query-performance tradeoffs, rather than a guarantee about measured total memory consumption. (medium confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-69899 · keywords: Cache-derived dynamic bucket size limit · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/v8.0/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp
- [statement] The v8.0 sizing function uses cache capacity and workload cardinality rather than current cache occupancy or eviction rate. Diagnose a rising cache-pressure bucket-closure counter alongside actual cache usage, configured cache capacity, and eviction metrics; the counter alone does not establish that WiredTiger cache is full. Percona documents those cache usage, capacity, and eviction dashboard panels. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/v8.0/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp · keywords: Cache-derived dynamic bucket size limit · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/reference/command/serverstatus/, https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/reference/dashboards/dashboard-mongodb-wiredtiger-details.html
- [statement] A 2023 user workload report describes roughly 25,000 buckets and 17 measurements per commit before concurrent loading, versus roughly 420,000 buckets, one measurement per commit, and 415,000 cache-pressure closures after loading other collections. SERVER-89233 separately records one-document bucket symptoms. These are historical workload observations, not expected outcomes for every deployment. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/suboptimal-bucket-creation-in-timeseries-collection-due-to-cache-pressure/249863 · keywords: Cache-derived dynamic bucket size limit · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-89233

## Facts and statements

- [statement] SERVER-69899 introduced dynamic sizing with fix version 6.2.0-rc0. Its stated aim was to keep active buckets within half the WiredTiger cache, reducing repeated disk writes at the cost of smaller buckets, greater disk usage, and potentially worse query performance. (medium confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-69899 · keywords: Cache-derived dynamic bucket size limit · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-105187
- [statement] In the v8.0 source examined, for cache capacity C and workload cardinality 0 < N < 2^31, getCacheDerivedBucketMaxSize computes D = max(gTimeseriesBucketMinSize, min(floor(C/(2*N)), INT32_MAX)) and returns {min(gTimeseriesBucketMaxSize, D), D}. For N = 0 it returns {gTimeseriesBucketMaxSize, INT_MAX}. The positive-N formula excludes unsigned overflow of 2 * workloadCardinality. This statement applies to that versioned source. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/v8.0/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp · keywords: Cache-derived dynamic bucket size limit · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-105187
- [statement] The minimum-size floor is historically version-sensitive. SERVER-82798 documents undersized buckets from the dynamic calculation and lists 7.0.4 and 7.2.0-rc0 as fix versions; the examined v8.0 code explicitly applies gTimeseriesBucketMinSize. These issue fields do not establish a complete backport matrix. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-21) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-82798 · keywords: Cache-derived dynamic bucket size limit · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/v8.0/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp
- [statement] SERVER-105187 describes raising the internal timeseriesBucketMinSize to timeseriesBucketMaxSize as effectively disabling dynamic sizing. Its request to make the calculation's slope configurable remains unresolved in the issue's July 14, 2025 update; this is an implementation discussion, not general production tuning guidance. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-07-14) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-105187
